- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR. # What does this PR do? Gives vocab-parallel cross entropy and normalization a home in `megatron/core/ops`, `ops/loss` and `ops/norm`, following the layout and rules of #7380 and of the SSM and attention moves in #7453 and #8348. Kernel integrations such as #5438 (Liger-Kernel RMSNorm and vocab-parallel cross entropy) then add an adapter module and a selector branch in these families instead of new files in `fusions/` and `extensions/`. Every old module path remains as a deprecated forwarder. **Based on `main`, ahead of the SSM move (#7453).** It has six commits and a merge of `main`: 1. `ops: write patches through deprecated forwarders and forward re-exported names`: #7453's first commit, unchanged. This move needs it too: without it, a patch written through an old path such as `megatron.core.fusions.fused_layer_norm` misses the implementation, and a `--spec` or checkpoint spec recorded under an old norm path stops loading. #7453 drops the commit once this PR lands. 2. `ops/loss, ops/norm: move vocab-parallel cross entropy and the norm modules into megatron/core/ops`: the move. 3. Review follow-ups, kept as separate commits on the reviewed head: - `ops: keep a patched name on its forwarder so nested patches undo by assignment`. A nested patch that set the outer patch's original back for a while lost the outer patch's record, and its exit deleted the implementation's attribute. A forwarder now holds a written name until the write ends, as a patched module does, so `mock.patch` and `monkeypatch` undo inner patches by assignment. - `training: keep private spec names in the inference-counterpart lookup`. The forwarder fallback skipped every underscore name, so a private `--spec` such as `_foo_stack_spec` no longer found `_foo_inference_stack_spec`. It now skips only dunder names. - `CODEOWNERS: give @NVIDIA/transformer all of megatron/core/ops/norm`, rather than `torch_norm.py` alone. - `ops: let a forwarder's first same-value write start a write`. Patching a name through an old path with the value it already held, as in `mock.patch.object(old_mod, "NAME", old_mod.NAME)`, raised `KeyError`. A write now ends only when one is in progress and the value is the one it replaced. 4. `Merge main into ops-move/loss-norm`: keeps both imports where #8399 added one next to a rewritten norm import in `deepseek_v4_hybrid_attention.py`. Since review started, `main` is merged in rather than regenerated, so the reviewed commits stay as they are. It is independent of #8348. The moved code is unchanged apart from imports, so open fixes to the old files, such as #7466's label-smoothing fix in `tensor_parallel/cross_entropy.py`, apply to the new paths once this lands. Like the other moves, the branch is **generated by a script** on `main` plus the helper commit rather than rebased, and is regenerated whenever `main` changes the moved files. Re-running the script reproduces the move commit apart from the manual steps listed below. ## Layout | Old (`megatron/core/`) | New (`megatron/core/`) | | --- | --- | | `tensor_parallel/cross_entropy.py` | `ops/loss/cross_entropy.py` | | `fusions/fused_cross_entropy.py` | `ops/loss/fused_cross_entropy.py` | | `models/backends.py`: `CrossEntropyTarget`, `select_cross_entropy` | `ops/loss/backends.py` | | `fusions/fused_layer_norm.py` | `ops/norm/fused_layer_norm.py` | | `transformer/torch_norm.py` | `ops/norm/torch_norm.py` | `ops/loss/__init__.py` and `ops/norm/__init__.py` hold each family's contract and re-export nothing. Transformer Engine's cross entropy and norms stay in `extensions/transformer_engine.py`, and `fused_gated_norm.py` (GDN's output norm) stays in `fusions/`. ## Where #5438's pieces go | #5438 adds | With this PR | | --- | --- | | `fusions/liger_cross_entropy.py` | `ops/loss/liger_cross_entropy.py`: an adapter with the `CrossEntropyTarget` signature `target(logits, labels, tp_group)` | | a `'liger'` arm in `LanguageModule.compute_language_model_loss` | a `'liger'` branch in `select_cross_entropy` (`ops/loss/backends.py`), the selector every provider asks. Since #6766, `LanguageModule` binds whatever that selector returns, so the model needs no change | | `'liger'` in `cross_entropy_fusion_impl` | unchanged; `select_cross_entropy` rejects values it does not know, so the value is added there too | | the `LigerMegatronRMSNorm` import in `extensions/liger_kernel_spec_provider.py` | `ops/norm/liger_norm.py`, which imports `liger_kernel` at module top; `LigerSpecProvider.layer_norm` returns it, and the provider and the `use_liger` spec plumbing stay in `extensions/` and `models/gpt` | | `HAVE_LIGER` flags and `try/except ImportError` | `require("liger_kernel.megatron", ..., needed_by=...)` in the selector branch, so the other values never import Liger and a missing package fails at construction | The new README section "Adding a cross-entropy or normalization backend" describes this without naming Liger. ## Compatibility - The four old module paths warn once and forward lazily. Patches written through them reach the implementation, and pickles and `(module, name)` specs recorded under them load the canonical objects (covered by the identity and pickle tests). - `from megatron.core.tensor_parallel import vocab_parallel_cross_entropy` and `from megatron.core.models.backends import CrossEntropyTarget, select_cross_entropy` keep working and return the same objects. - Importing `megatron.core.tensor_parallel` no longer binds the `cross_entropy` submodule as a package attribute. An explicit `import megatron.core.tensor_parallel.cross_entropy` still works, through the forwarder. No in-tree code relied on the attribute. - `select_cross_entropy` now reads `is_te_min_version` from `ops/loss/backends.py`, so a test that patched `megatron.core.models.backends.is_te_min_version` to steer it patches the new module instead. The two in-tree tests that did are updated. ## How it was generated ```bash git switch -c ops-move/loss-norm upstream/main git cherry-pick c80af85c5 # #7453's forwarder helper commit python ops_move_loss_norm.py # script below; template was the #8348 script ``` Manual steps after the script: - moved `CrossEntropyTarget` and `select_cross_entropy` verbatim from `models/backends.py` to `ops/loss/backends.py`; `models/backends.py`, the TE spec provider and `LanguageModule` import them from there; - `ops/norm/torch_norm.py` imports `TransformerConfig` for type checking only (it is used in annotations only). Outside the transformer package, the runtime import ran the package `__init__`, which reached `transformer_layer`, which imports `torch_norm` before it had finished loading, and `import megatron.core` failed. Inside the package, the package always initialized first; - the moved `fused_layer_norm.py` gets its four pylint fixes (an unused `importlib` import, a long comment, two method docstrings), because the linting job checks it as a new file; - `tools/check_kernel_determinism_coverage.py` does not count a deprecated forwarder left in a kernel directory as kernel-bearing. `fusions/` is one, and the forwarders there hold no kernel; the kernels are registered at their new paths. The alternative, manifest entries naming the old paths, would contradict the canonical-path test. A module with anything besides the forwarding call keeps the directory rule (tested). The manifest's `KERNEL_DIRECTORIES` comment also says why `megatron/core/ops` is not a kernel directory; - the README layout and the backend section, a `CODEOWNERS` line keeping `@NVIDIA/transformer` on `ops/norm/torch_norm.py`, and the re-sorted allowlist key in `tools/process_group_usage_allowlist.json`; - tests: identity and pickle cases for `VocabParallelCrossEntropy`, `FusedLayerNorm`, `WrappedTorchNorm` and `L2Norm`; the package export and the selector's old import path; the forwarder rule of the coverage tool; the `torch_norm.py` path in the `test_fused_activations.py` docstring; - `isort` on the changed Python files and `black` on those under `megatron/core` and `tests`. Verify the move: `git diff -M -C --find-copies-harder 577586474~1 577586474` shows the moved modules as `C092`–`C099`. Two have one import line changed; `fused_layer_norm.py` and `torch_norm.py` carry the edits above.
ops_move_loss_norm.py ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Move vocab-parallel cross entropy and the normalization modules into ``megatron/core/ops``. Run from the repository root on a clean checkout of ``main`` with the forwarder helper commit (``ops: write patches through deprecated forwarders ...``) applied:: python ops_move_loss_norm.py The script only moves files (``git mv``), rewrites import paths and path strings, and writes the forwarder modules, the new package docstrings and the ``FORWARDED`` entries. Formatting (isort, black) runs afterwards. """ from __future__ import annotations import ast import importlib.util import re import subprocess from pathlib import Path ROOT = Path.cwd() CORE = "megatron/core" # Old module file -> new module file, relative to megatron/core. Only whole modules move; no # old package moves, so no old package needs a forwarder of its own. FILE_MOVES = { "tensor_parallel/cross_entropy.py": "ops/loss/cross_entropy.py", "fusions/fused_cross_entropy.py": "ops/loss/fused_cross_entropy.py", "fusions/fused_layer_norm.py": "ops/norm/fused_layer_norm.py", "transformer/torch_norm.py": "ops/norm/torch_norm.py", } # Docstrings of the new canonical packages; each holds its contract and re-exports nothing. NEW_PACKAGES = { "ops/loss": ( "Vocab-parallel cross entropy.\n\n" "A target is called as ``loss = target(logits, labels, tp_group)`` with ``logits``\n" "``[s, b, vocab / tp]`` and ``labels`` ``[s, b]``, and returns the per-token loss\n" "``[s, b]``. The target owns every reduction over ``tp_group`` and consumes ``logits``\n" "in place; ``backends.CrossEntropyTarget`` states the contract. Targets hold no\n" "parameters or state.\n\n" "* ``cross_entropy`` -- the eager custom-autograd implementation, with label smoothing,\n" " and the ``VocabParallelCrossEntropy`` steps the fused path shares.\n" "* ``fused_cross_entropy`` -- the same computation compiled with ``jit_fuser``.\n" "* ``backends`` -- ``select_cross_entropy``, which turns ``cross_entropy_loss_fusion``\n" " and ``cross_entropy_fusion_impl`` into the target a model binds once.\n\n" "Transformer Engine's cross entropy stays in ``megatron.core.extensions.transformer_engine``.\n" "Packages here do not re-export; import each name from the module that defines it.\n" ), "ops/norm": ( "Normalization modules.\n\n" "A norm is built through a ``torch_norm.LayerNormBuilder``,\n" "``target(config=..., hidden_size=..., eps=...)``, and satisfies\n" "``torch_norm.LayerNormInterface``: ``forward(x)`` normalizes over the last dimension and\n" "``returns_residual`` says whether it also returns the residual it fused. A model's\n" "``BackendSpecProvider.layer_norm`` chooses the builder. A norm owns its parameters\n" "(``weight``, plus ``bias`` for LayerNorm; ``L2Norm`` has none) and no process groups.\n\n" "* ``torch_norm`` -- the builder protocols, ``WrappedTorchNorm`` (PyTorch LayerNorm and\n" " RMSNorm) and ``L2Norm``.\n" "* ``fused_layer_norm`` -- Apex's fused LayerNorm, ``FusedLayerNorm``.\n\n" "Transformer Engine's norms stay in ``megatron.core.extensions.transformer_engine``.\n" "Packages here do not re-export; import each name from the module that defines it.\n" ), } # Text files whose path strings and dotted module names are rewritten. REWRITE_SUFFIXES = {".py", ".md", ".sh", ".json", ".yaml", ".yml", ".rst", ".txt"} # The deprecated-path regression suite names the old paths on purpose; it is edited by hand. SKIP_PREFIXES = ("tests/unit_tests/ops/", "CHANGELOG.md") COPYRIGHT = "# Copyright (c) 2026, NVIDIA CORPORATION. All rights reserved.\n" def dotted(path: str) -> str: """``megatron/core/a/b/__init__.py`` -> ``megatron.core.a.b``.""" path = path[: -len(".py")] if path.endswith(".py") else path path = path[: -len("/__init__")] if path.endswith("/__init__") else path return path.replace("/", ".") MOVES = {f"{CORE}/{old}": f"{CORE}/{new}" for old, new in FILE_MOVES.items()} RENAMES = {dotted(old): dotted(new) for old, new in MOVES.items()} # Packages that lose a module; their files may import it relatively, without naming megatron. OLD_PACKAGE_DIRS = tuple(sorted({str(Path(old).parent) + "/" for old in MOVES})) def map_module(name: str) -> str: """Map a dotted name through the longest moved module prefix.""" parts = name.split(".") for i in range(len(parts), 0, -1): prefix = ".".join(parts[:i]) if prefix in RENAMES: return ".".join([RENAMES[prefix], *parts[i:]]) return name _OLD = "|".join(re.escape(old) for old in sorted(RENAMES, key=len, reverse=True)) _OLD_PATHS = "|".join(re.escape(old.replace(".", "/")) for old in sorted(RENAMES, key=len, reverse=True)) DOTTED_RE = re.compile(rf"(? str: text = match.group(0) is_file = text.endswith(".py") stem = text[: -len(".py")] if is_file else text new = RENAMES[stem.replace("/", ".")].replace(".", "/") return f"{new}.py" if is_file else new def package_of(path: str) -> str: return dotted(str(Path(path).parent)) def resolve(node: ast.ImportFrom, package: str) -> str: if not node.level: return node.module or "" return importlib.util.resolve_name("." * node.level + (node.module or ""), package) def relative_to(source: str, package: str) -> str: """Spell ``source`` relative to ``package`` when it lives in that package.""" if source == package: return "." if source.startswith(package + "."): return "." + source[len(package) + 1 :] return source def rewrite_import_statements(path: str, text: str, new_path: str | None) -> str: """Rewrite import statements that a textual prefix substitution cannot express. * ``from import moved_module`` binds the moved module under its old name. * Relative imports keep their form when they still resolve after the move; otherwise they become relative to the file's new package, or absolute when the target is outside. """ try: tree = ast.parse(text) except SyntaxError: return text lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True) old_package = package_of(path) new_package = package_of(new_path) if new_path else old_package edits = [] for node in ast.walk(tree): if not isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom): continue module = resolve(node, old_package) indent = re.match(r"\s*", lines[node.lineno - 1]).group(0) groups: dict[str, list[str]] = {} if node.level and map_module(module) == module and all( f"{resolve(node, new_package)}.{alias.name}" == map_module(f"{module}.{alias.name}") for alias in node.names ): # The relative import still names the same modules and objects after the move. continue if any(f"{module}.{alias.name}" in RENAMES for alias in node.names): for alias in node.names: full = f"{module}.{alias.name}" if full in RENAMES: parent, _, base = RENAMES[full].rpartition(".") local = alias.asname or alias.name groups.setdefault(parent, []).append( base if base == local else f"{base} as {local}" ) else: groups.setdefault(map_module(module), []).append( alias.name + (f" as {alias.asname}" if alias.asname else "") ) elif node.level: names = [a.name + (f" as {a.asname}" if a.asname else "") for a in node.names] groups[map_module(module)] = names else: continue if node.level: groups = {relative_to(source, new_package): names for source, names in groups.items()} statement = "".join( f"{indent}from {source} import {', '.join(names)}\n" for source, names in groups.items() ) edits.append((node.lineno, node.end_lineno, statement)) for start, end, statement in sorted(edits, reverse=True): lines[start - 1 : end] = [statement] return "".join(lines) # ``from import `` written out in text, such as a code string run # in a subprocess; real import statements were already rewritten from the syntax tree. _OLD_PARENTS = "|".join(re.escape(p) for p in sorted({o.rpartition(".")[0] for o in RENAMES})) FROM_IMPORT_RE = re.compile( rf"\bfrom ({_OLD_PARENTS}) import (\w+)(?: as (\w+))?(?=\s*$)", re.MULTILINE ) def map_from_import(match: re.Match) -> str: module, name, alias = match.groups() if f"{module}.{name}" not in RENAMES: return match.group(0) parent, _, base = RENAMES[f"{module}.{name}"].rpartition(".") local = alias or name return f"from {parent} import {base}" + ("" if base == local else f" as {local}") def rewrite_text(text: str) -> str: text = FROM_IMPORT_RE.sub(map_from_import, text) text = DOTTED_RE.sub(lambda m: map_module(m.group(0)), text) return PATH_RE.sub(map_path, text) def forwarder(old: str, new: str) -> str: doc = f'"""Deprecated import path; use ``{new}``."""' if len(doc) > 100: doc = f'"""Deprecated import path.\n\nUse ``{new}``.\n"""' return ( f"{COPYRIGHT}\n{doc}\n\n" "from megatron.core.ops._compat import deprecated_module\n\n" f'__getattr__, __dir__ = deprecated_module(__name__, "{new}")\n' ) def package_init(doc: str) -> str: # A one-line docstring closes on its own line; a longer one closes on the line after. doc = doc.rstrip("\n") if "\n" not in doc.rstrip("\n") else doc return f'{COPYRIGHT}\n"""{doc}"""\n' def forwarded_entries() -> str: return "".join(f' "{old}": ("{new}",),\n' for old, new in RENAMES.items()) def git(*args: str) -> str: return subprocess.run(["git", *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout def main() -> None: assert not git("status", "--porcelain"), "run on a clean checkout" tracked = git("ls-files").splitlines() # 1. Rewrite every tracked text file in place (moved files keep their old location for now). for path in tracked: if path.startswith(SKIP_PREFIXES) or Path(path).suffix not in REWRITE_SUFFIXES: continue file = ROOT / path original = file.read_text() if "megatron" not in original and not path.startswith(OLD_PACKAGE_DIRS): continue text = original if path.endswith(".py"): text = rewrite_import_statements(path, text, MOVES.get(path)) text = rewrite_text(text) if text != original: file.write_text(text) # 2. Create the new packages, then move. for package, doc in NEW_PACKAGES.items(): init = ROOT / CORE / package / "__init__.py" init.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) init.write_text(package_init(doc)) git("add", str(init.relative_to(ROOT))) for old, new in MOVES.items(): git("mv", old, new) # 3. Leave a forwarder at every old path. for old, new in MOVES.items(): (ROOT / old).write_text(forwarder(dotted(old), dotted(new))) git("add", old) # 4. Record the forwarders in the regression table. table = ROOT / "tests/unit_tests/ops/deprecated_paths.py" # The first family to move finds the table empty, written on one line. text = table.read_text().replace("FORWARDED = {}\n", "FORWARDED = {\n}\n", 1) head, sep, tail = text.partition("\n}\n") assert sep and head.lstrip().startswith("#") and "FORWARDED = {" in head, "unexpected table" table.write_text(head + "\n" + forwarded_entries().rstrip("\n") + sep + tail) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```

Found two localized compatibility regressions: nested patch restoration can delete a canonical attribute, and private HybridStack spec names no longer resolve their inference counterparts. Details and acceptance checks are inline.

Completed the light review across all changed files and directly affected paths. This was static inspection; no tests were executed.

<!-- nemo-ci-formal-review:a2bbbd943d7aa02d177c191c7799e2d2a819d0e6e4abfff73a8dacc0c473fc3b:ee978770baa62afdfa987aa0f6f84c5cb3ea1d5ebfb343ec847ca72a80491bce -->

[P2] Preserve nested patches that temporarily restore the original value

**Failure:** Let `alias` be a single-target deprecated forwarder, `canonical` its implementation, and `canonical.public` initially hold `original`. This valid nesting breaks restoration:
```python
replacement = object()
with mock.patch.object(alias, "public", replacement):
    with mock.patch.object(alias, "public", original, create=True):
        pass
    assert canonical.public is replacement
```
The inner assignment equals `replaced[-1]`, so [the setter](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/57758647411d94bfaa8a663b42127786fc397740/megatron/core/ops/_compat.py#L63-L69) pops the outer rollback frame instead of recording the inner patch. On inner exit, [the empty-stack deletion branch](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/57758647411d94bfaa8a663b42127786fc397740/megatron/core/ops/_compat.py#L71-L84) deletes `canonical.public`. With `create=True`, `mock.patch` does not subsequently reassign the saved value, leaving the attribute absent and potentially breaking outer teardown too.

**Correction:** Revise `__setattr__`/`__delattr__` bookkeeping so every newly entered patch retains its rollback state even when its replacement equals a previously saved value. Value identity alone cannot distinguish patch entry from setter-based undo. A safe drop-in implementation is uncertain because simply removing this shortcut also changes the older `monkeypatch.undo()` setter behavior; the fix must preserve both restoration contracts.

**Preservation and acceptance:** Extend [the existing patch regression](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/57758647411d94bfaa8a663b42127786fc397740/tests/unit_tests/ops/test_deprecated_imports.py#L140-L175) with the example above: expect `replacement` after the inner scope and `original` after the outer scope, without exceptions. Retain the existing distinct-replacement nesting and `monkeypatch.undo()` assertions. Also check that patching a previously absent name with `create=True` removes it on exit, while local child-module bindings remain local and ambiguous multi-target writes still raise. These are proposed checks, not executed results.

+            # So we can just take the log to get log-probs.

+            )

+        return grad_input, None, None, None
+

+def vocab_parallel_cross_entropy(

+    label_smoothing: float = 0.0,
+    tp_group: torch.distributed.ProcessGroup | None = None,

+    return _VocabParallelCrossEntropy.apply(
